questions.question: How does an attempt actually work?
questions.answer: Questions come one at a time. Answer, press **Next** — **Finish** on the last one — and the server keeps each answer as you go. Nothing is lost if the tab closes.

questions.question: What should I take a test on?
questions.answer: A laptop or desktop with a current Chrome, Edge or Firefox. Phones and tablets work, but a small screen can make long questions harder to read.

questions.question: The page froze or will not open.
questions.answer: Check your connection and reload. If it persists, clear the browser cache or try another device — your attempt is on the server, not in the tab.

questions.question: Which question types can appear?
questions.answer: Single choice, multiple choice, essay, and matching pairs.

questions.question: Can I go back to a previous question?
questions.answer: Usually not. Check your answer before you press **Next**.

questions.question: What happens when the time runs out?
questions.answer: The attempt closes itself. Everything you had already answered is kept.

questions.question: Can I retake a test?
questions.answer: Only if your instructor or an administrator opens a new attempt for you.

questions.question: Why can I not see my mark?
questions.answer: Marks appear only if your instructor turned that on. Otherwise you see your own answers without scoring.

questions.question: What can I see after I finish?
questions.answer: Your own answers, always. Correct answers and a mark only if your instructor allows it.

questions.question: An error appeared when the test started.
questions.answer: Reload the page. The session is restored from the server, and the clock has not been running against you in the meantime.

questions.question: How is my attempt monitored?
questions.answer: Tab switches, copy events and disconnects are logged and sent with your result. Nothing else about your device is recorded.

transfer.lede: StudEase expects schemaVersion: 1, a kind, and the payload in data or items. Old ids, session counts and anything the server computes are not needed — it creates fresh records.

guideCards.title: Export one test or collection
guideCards.text: Open Tests or Collections, use the actions on the row or card, and choose Export. StudEase downloads a JSON file you can import back later.

guideCards.title: Export several at once
guideCards.text: Switch the second segmented control to Select, tick what you need, and press Export. You get one bundle file with an items array.

guideCards.title: Import a single item
guideCards.text: Press Import on Tests or Collections and choose the JSON. A file with one item opens the create form with the fields already filled in.

guideCards.title: Import a bundle
guideCards.text: A file with several items is created straight away. Import a bundle of tests from Tests, and a bundle of collections from Collections.
